abstract_sentences.text: Large language models (LLMs) must balance diversity and creativity against logical coherence in open-ended generation.

evidence.anchor: Large language models (LLMs) must balance diversity and creativity

abstract_sentences.text: Existing truncation-based samplers are effective but largely heuristic, relying mainly on probability mass and entropy while ignoring semantic geometry of the token space.

evidence.anchor: Existing truncation-based samplers are effective but largely heuristic

abstract_sentences.transition: turns the trade-off into a gap

abstract_sentences.text: We present Top-W, a geometry-aware truncation rule that uses Wasserstein distance—defined over token-embedding geometry—to keep the cropped distribution close to the original, while explicitly balancing retained probability mass against the entropy of the kept set.

evidence.anchor: We present Top-W, a geometry-aware truncation rule

abstract_sentences.text: Our theory yields a simple closed-form structure for the fixed-potential subset update: depending on the mass–entropy trade-off, the optimal crop either collapses to a single token or takes the form of a one-dimensional prefix that can be found efficiently with a linear scan.

evidence.anchor: the optimal crop either collapses to a single token

abstract_sentences.transition: moves from method to structure theorem

abstract_sentences.text: We implement Top-W using efficient geometry-based potentials (nearest-set or k-NN) and pair it with an alternating decoding routine that keeps the standard truncation-and-sampling interface unchanged.

evidence.anchor: pair it with an alternating decoding routine

abstract_sentences.transition: turns the structure into an implementation

abstract_sentences.text: Extensive experiments on four benchmarks (GSM8K, GPQA, AlpacaEval, and MT-Bench) across three instruction-tuned models show that Top-W consistently outperforms prior state-of-the-art decoding approaches achieving up to 33.7% improvement.
Moreover, we find that Top-W not only improves accuracy-focused performance, but also boosts creativity under judge-based open-ended evaluation.

evidence.anchor: also boosts creativity under judge-based open-ended evaluation

abstract_sentences.transition: extends the claimed benefit to creativity

experimental_design.name: benchmarks_and_metrics

claim_closure.claim: Embedding geometry improves truncation by preserving semantically nearby mass while balancing entropy and retained mass.
claim_closure.method_response: Eq. (1), Eq. (5), and f_S=-dist(i,S) make the intended mechanism explicit.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Multi-benchmark performance is reported, but no direct measurement of semantic transport preservation or a mediator test is reported.

evidence.anchor: embedding space where distances encode graded semantic similarity

claim_closure.claim: For fixed feasible potential f, the subset update has an exact efficient prefix/singleton structure.
claim_closure.method_response: Lemma 3.2 defines G_f and Theorem 3.4 states prefix versus singleton regimes.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Appendix B.1/C/D provide algebraic proofs and monotonicity for the fixed-f setting.

evidence.anchor: Fixed-f surrogate and proof of Lemma 3.2

claim_closure.claim: The objective connects to Top-k and Top-H under uniform-metric specializations.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Appendix H proves W1=1-Gamma_S and derives the Top-k and Top-H cases.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §8 refers to specializations to standard decoding rules.

claim_closure.claim: Top-W consistently outperforms strong decoding baselines across four benchmarks.
claim_closure.method_response: Algorithm 1 and fixed configuration instantiate the method.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Tables/Figures show 13/15, 12/15, 12/15, and 8/15 aggregate wins; some source baselines are quoted and uncertainty reporting is limited.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §8 says Top-W wins in a large majority of cases.

claim_closure.claim: Top-W boosts creativity under judge-based open-ended evaluation.
claim_closure.method_response: beta is presented as a knob controlling viable support and exploration.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 3 gives 9/27 default wins and Appendix Table 8 gives 12/27 for a changed beta schedule; outcomes vary by model/prompt.

evidence.anchor: boosts creativity under judge-based open-ended evaluation

claim_closure.claim: Top-W retains the standard truncation-and-sampling interface with modest overhead.
claim_closure.method_response: Algorithm 1 is a logits processor and masks nonselected logits.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Appendix K provides complexity and Table 4 provides limited ms/token measurements.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §8 calls the implementation suitable for a logits processor.

limitations.name: exact_kr_infeasibility
limitations.description: Exact KR dual LP has Theta(n^2) Lipschitz constraints and is infeasible at vocabulary scale; implementation uses a feasible-potential alternating surrogate.

final_judgment.single_storyline: Top-W replaces probability/entropy-only support selection with an embedding-geometry-aware W1–entropy–mass objective, then turns a combinatorial crop search into a fixed-f prefix scan usable by a logits processor. [PDF pp. 2–5, §1–4]
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The main body retains the objective, six named theory results, Algorithm 1, default settings, task-level aggregate results, and beta sensitivity; a reader can identify the algorithmic decision without Appendix A–M. [PDF pp. 3–9, §3–8]
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Proofs, exact-KR cost rationale, candidate-pool condition, detailed protocol, tuning grid, judge prompt, runtime cells, and per-model creative heterogeneity move to Appendix A–M. This preserves a readable main story but requires appendices to assess assumptions and reproducibility. [PDF pp. 11–20, Appendix A–M]
final_judgment.best_pattern: The paper stages Eq. (5) as the three-way objective, Eq. (8)–(13) as the exact fixed-f reduction, and Algorithm 1 as the executable loop; each stage answers the prior computation barrier. [PDF pp. 3–5, §3–4]
final_judgment.largest_gap: The performance evidence does not directly test whether embedding geometry preserves semantic continuity, and the global behavior of the complete alternating loop is not a theorem of the fixed-f result. Aggregate winner counts also require reading Appendix M for creative heterogeneity. [PDF pp. 4–5, §3–4; pp. 18–20, Appendix M]
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For a combinatorial support-selection method, connect an interpretable objective to a provably scanable restricted subproblem, make that subproblem operational in the deployed loop, and test parameter predictions on bounded task settings. [PDF pp. 3–5, §3–4; pp. 7–9, §6.2]
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: State separately what is exact for the restricted subproblem and what is only empirically supported for the full implementation, especially when feasible potentials, candidate pools, or alternations change the original optimization. [PDF pp. 13–16, Appendix E/I/K]

evidence_coverage.coverage_rule: Every substantive structured fact and judgement above has at least one physical-PDF page, section, and short anchor; inability to establish a fact is coded not_present or annotated uncertain.
